transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because... honestly, I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. 

It all started when these foreclosure notices began showing up in the mail. Ever since they started coming, I just haven't been right. I find myself sitting out in my truck crying before my shift even starts, and I jump every single time my phone rings. 

It's really messing with my work, too. I'm snapping at the apprentices, and I'm making these stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never, ever would have made before all this. I just need some help getting a grip on things.

Are you finding that your anxiety and worry are primarily focused on the financial situation and the threat of losing your home, or do you find yourself feeling anxious about a wide range of different things in your daily life?

Honestly, it's really just the house and the money. I mean, before those letters started coming, I was fine. I've never been someone who worries about a bunch of random things in my daily life. 

It's just... well, it's this one massive problem hanging over my head. I'm not stressing about everyday stuff or anything like that, it's just the thought of losing my home. That's what is constantly on my mind and keeping me tied up in knots.
About how long ago did you receive that first foreclosure notice?

I don't have the exact day in front of me, but... well, I know I was functioning completely normally until those letters and the phone calls started. Everything was fine before that. But within just a few weeks of getting that first formal notice, my work and my home life just started unraveling.
Beyond the anxiety and irritability you mentioned, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, your sleep, or your ability to find pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Sleep is definitely a problem. I just lie there thinking about the house and the bank, running numbers in my head. I'm exhausted, but I can't turn my brain off. As for my appetite... I don't know, I guess I'm just not eating as much. Food doesn't really sound good right now. And things I used to enjoy? I don't even have the energy to care about them anymore. I used to like working on my own truck on the weekends, but now I just sit in the living room staring at the wall.
Do you feel that the level of distress you are experiencing is disproportionate to the situation you are facing?

I don't know if I'd say it's disproportionate. I mean, losing my house is a pretty massive deal. It feels like my whole life is falling apart, so being this stressed out about it seems... well, it seems like the normal way to react to something this bad. I don't feel like I'm overreacting, if that's what you mean. It's just a really terrible situation.
Do you feel that your current level of distress is causing you to struggle significantly more than other people might in this same situation?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I don't know how other people would handle this. I just know that for me, it's completely overwhelming. I don't feel like I'm handling it well at all, but I don't have anything to compare it to.
Since those first notices arrived, have there been any days where you felt you were handling the situation well, or has this feeling of being overwhelmed been present every single day?

I don't think there's been a single good day since this started. It's just been a constant weight, every single day. I wake up and it's right there waiting for me. I haven't had a break from feeling like this since those first letters showed up.
About how many months has it been since you received that first notice?
It's been... about four months now. Yeah, right around four months since those first foreclosure notices started coming in.
Over the past four months, have you felt sad, empty, or down in the dumps for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty all the time. It's more just... stress, you know? Like this heavy pressure about the house and the money. I don't sit around feeling down in the dumps or crying all day. It's just the constant worry about what's going to happen that's overwhelming me.

When you are not actively thinking about the house or the money, do you find that thoughts or memories of the situation ever pop into your mind against your will, or do you have any physical reactions, like a racing heart or shaking, when you are reminded of the foreclosure?

No, I wouldn't say that happens. I mean, I'm pretty much always thinking about it anyway because it's a massive problem I have to figure out. But it doesn't just flash into my mind against my will or anything like that. And I don't get the shakes or a racing heart when I think about it. It's just... it's just a constant, heavy stress I can't seem to shake off.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels, such as feeling physically slowed down or having a hard time getting yourself to move, over these past four months?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired because I'm stressed out and not sleeping great, but I don't feel physically slowed down or anything. I can still get up and move around fine, and do my job at the shop... it's just hard to focus sometimes. But physically, my energy is mostly the same.
Even though you don't feel 'down in the dumps,' have you lost interest or pleasure in almost all of your daily activities during these past four months?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in everything. I still like doing my usual stuff. I mean... it's hard to fully relax and enjoy things right now with this whole house situation hanging over my head, but I haven't stopped caring about my life or the things I normally like to do. I still get enjoyment out of my day-to-day things, it's just that the stress is always there in the background.
Even though you don't feel 'down in the dumps,' have you experienced any episodes of crying or feelings of sadness since this situation began?

Well, yeah, I have been crying. Ever since those foreclosure notices started showing up, I just feel like I'm coming apart at the seams. I've been crying in my truck before work. And I'm just so on edge... I jump every time the phone rings. I've been snapping at the apprentices at the shop, which isn't like me. And I'm making stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would've made before all this started. It's just really getting to me.

When you think about the way you've been feeling over these last few months, would you say that the feeling of anxiety and being on edge is the main problem, or is the feeling of sadness and the crying just as significant to you?

I honestly don't know if I can separate them. The anxiety and being on edge is definitely constant, just... waiting for the next shoe to drop with the house. But the crying and feeling so overwhelmed by the sadness, that feels just as significant to me. 

It's like they go hand in hand right now. I wouldn't say one is the main problem over the other... they're both just really making it hard to get through the day.

When you are crying or feeling that deep sense of being overwhelmed, do you feel that it is primarily coming from a place of fear and worry about the future, or does it feel more like a heavy, hopeless, or low mood?

I guess... I don't really know how to answer that. I haven't really stopped to think about exactly where it's coming from. I just know I feel terrible. It's probably a mix of both, but I couldn't say for sure if it's more fear or more of a low mood. I just know it's there.
When you are feeling these moments of being overwhelmed, do you ever feel a sense of hopelessness or a lack of self-worth that is separate from your fear about the foreclosure?

No, not really. I mean... I don't feel worthless. I know I'm good at my job, even with the mistakes lately, and I know I'm a good person. It's not about me being... bad or anything. It's just the situation. The foreclosure. If that wasn't happening, I wouldn't be feeling this way at all. I don't feel hopeless about life in general, just... backed into a corner right now with the house.
